# MIGRATION SPEC — MCP Python SDK v1 → v2

(As given verbatim to each Target B detection agent on 2026-08-18. The
original session's spec text was never persisted anywhere on disk, so this
is a recons

facts.text: The module path `mcp.server.fastmcp` is removed entirely in v2. Everything that lived there moves to `mcp.server.mcpserver`. Any `from mcp.server.fastmcp import X` or `import mcp.server.fastmcp` must become `from mcp.server.mcpserver import X` (respectively the `mcp.server.mcpserver` module path).

The main server class `FastMCP` is renamed to `MCPServer`. `FastMCP` no longer exists under that name anywhere in the package. Every place that imports it, uses it as a type annotation, subclasses it, or constructs it (`FastMCP(...)`) must have the identifier itself changed to `MCPServer` — this is a real class rename, not only an import-path change.

The `Context` class moves with the rest of the module — `from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context` becomes `from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context` — but `Context` KEEPS its own name. Nothing else about `Context` changes: its methods, its behavior, and its use as a type annotation elsewhere are all unaffected. Do not rename `Context`.

On the MCP client side, tool metadata objects returned by the SDK change field-naming convention from camelCase to snake_case: `tool.inputSchema` is renamed to `tool.input_schema`. Client code reading `.inputSchema` off a discovered tool object must change.
`ClientSessionGroup.call_tool()` (the class managing calls across a group of client sessions) has a changed calling contract in v2.
Plain `ClientSession.call_tool()` on a single session is UNCHANGED — do not conflate it with `ClientSessionGroup.call_tool()`.

The SDK's own internal HTTP transport dependency changed from the `httpx` package to `httpx2`. This is purely internal to the SDK's implementation and has zero relevance to application code that imports and uses the separate `httpx` package for its own purposes (e.g. unrelated HTTP calls). Ordinary application-level `httpx` usage must NOT be flagged.
CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: the `@mcp.tool()`, `@mcp.resource()`, and `@mcp.prompt()` decorators have identical signature and behavior in v2.

CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: `ctx.error(...)` / `ctx.info(...)` calls that do NOT pass an `extra=` keyword argument are unchanged. (Calls that DO pass `extra=` have a different, changed signature, but plain calls without `extra=` are to be treated as unaffected.)
CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: anything imported from `mcp.types` — this subpackage remains aliased and working in v2.
The listed items are the ONLY confirmed changes; anything not described in the spec is unaffected by the migration.

Affected sites include ones reached indirectly through a repo's own helper functions and through test files, and also string literals that reference the old module path `mcp.server.fastmcp` (e.g. inside test mocks/patch targets).
